_about: Numerical values from Tsuda et al. (2026), stored for reference and comparison. Each block has 'source': 'table' / 'text' are exact values printed in the paper (page given); 'figure' values were READ BY EYE from the figures of the J-STAGE PDF rendered at 220 dpi and are approximate (estimated reading uncertainty in 'uncertainty'). Transcribed 2026-11-02.

citation.title_ja: X線マイクロCTを用いた繊維配向分布に基づく短繊維強化樹脂の残留応力解析
citation.title_en: Residual Stress Analysis of Short Fiber Reinforced Plastic Based on Fiber Orientation Distribution Measured Using X-ray Micro-CT
citation.journal: 日本複合材料学会誌 (Journal of the Japan Society for Composite Materials)

material.phases: PPS and GF both isotropic thermoelastic

processing.evaluation_site: 50 mm from the film gate; in-plane orientation assumed uniform, through-thickness distribution only

table1_PPS_inverse.note: PPS Young's modulus and instantaneous CTE identified by inverse analysis of the FRP tests; linearly interpolated between temperatures in the residual-stress analysis

methods.ct: synchrotron X-ray micro-CT at Aichi SR, voxel 2.66 x 2.66 x 2.66 um, VGSTUDIO MAX; second-order a_ij through thickness
methods.homogenisation: Mori-Tanaka mean field (Digimat-MF), closure approximation for a_ijkl (type not stated)
methods.tensile: 1.0 mm plate, MD and TD, RT(=20), 80, 100, 180 C, N = 2 each, gauges on both faces averaged
methods.tma: 5.0 mm square, 0-180 C, MD then TD on the same sample; instantaneous CTE by 10 C central differences
methods.inverse_fe: 5 x 5 mm, 20 um element layers (54 layers for 1.08 mm)
methods.residual_fe: Abaqus; 20 x 20 mm region of the 3.0 mm plate, 20 um layers (154 layers for 3.08 mm); thermal strain eps_th = alpha (T - T0) I; T0 = 180 C (anneal temperature, assumed for convenience); uniform cooling to RT
methods.hole_drilling: Tokyo Measuring Instruments FRAS-2 rosette; phi 1.6 mm drill; to 2.0 mm depth in 0.2 mm steps; 20 x 20 mm specimen; simulated by setting element stiffness to 0 per 0.2 mm (UMAT); released strain E_rel = E_el,after - E_el,before averaged over each gauge area

results_text.skin_definition: depth where a_xx > a_yy turns into a_xx < a_yy

surface_centre_residual_stress_MPa.note: at the centre of the drilled surface; x = MD compressive, y = TD tensile

results_text.crystallinity_argument: ref. 17 (Imaizumi et al., Seikei-Kakou 22 (2010) 590): 3 mm PPS cylinder moulded at 320 C; mould <= 90 C leaves the surface under-crystallised, mould >= 120 C gives nearly uniform crystallinity; hence the authors judge the crystallinity effect small for their conditions
results_text.conclusion_qualitative: fibre orientation distribution and the resulting anisotropic thermoelastic properties
results_text.conclusion_quantitative: the temperature change that contributes to thermal stress (cooling process, simultaneous stress build-up and relaxation)

fig7_orientation_1mm.symmetry: approximately symmetric about z = 0; values given for z <= 0

off_diagonal_peaks.a_xy: +0.08 near 1.2 mm, -0.12 near 2.4 mm, down to -0.17 at 3.08 mm

fig9_stress_strain_secant.note: secant modulus = stress / strain at the end of each curve, in GPa; experiments slightly non-linear, simulations linear

fig12_released_strain.gauges: Ch.1 along TD, Ch.2 at 45 deg, Ch.3 along MD (FRAS-2 rosette)
